summary: auth set-token writes the credentials file colocated with an explicit --config when it exists (the file Load reads first); auth logout removes only the credentials file that config uses and, when Load (via --config or WAVESPEED_CONFIG) still falls back to the separate default login, says so instead of implying the CLI is logged out; auth set-token also accepts the legacy positional token with a stdin warning.
reason: The generated save path always used the global credentials file, so with an explicit --config that had its own data/credentials.toml set-token reported success while the old token stayed active. Logout of one config must not log the user out of their default account. Earlier releases took the token positionally; rejecting it would break existing scripts.
validated_outcome: TestSetTokenWritesExplicitConfigCredentials, TestSetTokenAcceptsLegacyPositionalToken and TestLogoutClearsOnlyTheSelectedLogin (logout via WAVESPEED_CONFIG keeps and reports the default login; plain logout clears it).
